items.title: iv. Reactions of Halogenoalkanes with Aqueous Silver Nitrate

source_refs.note: iv. Reactions of Halogenoalkanes with Aqueous Silver Nitrate: a main subheading of 21.4 Examples of Reactions of Halogenoalkanes, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 82-84.

blocks.text: This reaction is carried out in a mixture of water and ethanol, the alcohol in this mixture helps to dissolve the halogenoalkane. Water reacts with halogenoalkane as a nucleophile replacing the halide ion.

The released halide ion then reacts with silver nitrate to give a precipitate with a characteristic colour corresponding to the halide ion present. Thus, the reaction helps to detect the halide ion present in halogenoalkanes.

Comparing the rates of formation of silver halides in this reaction gives us a clue about the different reactivities of halides. The quicker the precipitate appears, the more reactive is the halogenoalkane. An iodoalkane produces a precipitate very quicker than bromoalkane. A chloroalkane, however, reacts very slowly.

blocks.prompt: a) Why halogenoalkanes are considered as very reactive class of organic compounds?
blocks.explanation: The C–X bond is polar, so the carbon is electrophilic (δ+) and is a target for nucleophiles; the halide ion is a good leaving group; and the C–Cl, C–Br and C–I bonds are relatively weak. Bases can also remove HX to form alkenes.

blocks.prompt: b) Complete the following equation. C₂H₅Br + CH₃COONa →
blocks.explanation: C₂H₅Br + CH₃COONa → CH₃COOC₂H₅ (ethyl ethanoate) + NaBr. The ethanoate ion (CH₃COO⁻) acts as the nucleophile.

blocks.prompt: c) How will you convert ethane into ethanol and ethene?
blocks.explanation: First, ethane + Cl₂ in light → chloroethane + HCl. Then heat chloroethane with aqueous NaOH to get ethanol, or with NaOH in ethanol (alcohol) to get ethene.

blocks.prompt: d) Give the reaction of bromopropane with KCN. Is this a substitution reaction or an elimination reaction? Name the main product of this reaction.
blocks.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂Br + KCN → CH₃CH₂CH₂CN + KBr (in ethanol, under reflux). It is a nucleophilic substitution; the main product is butanenitrile.
